title: cost-optimization-autotune-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling-enhancements
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Introduces autotune defaults for batching and caching, adds quantization profiles for common workload archetypes, and exposes unit-economics metrics in the Optimize tooling; backward compatible by default; no manual migration required
body: Motivation: Reduce per-token cost and operator overhead by shipping production-ready defaults and tooling to autotune batching/caching/quantization per workload. This PR implements an end-to-end flow: 1) new default heuristics that pick batching and KV cache TTLs based on request size distribution and SLO targets, 2) a set of quantization profiles (int8/int4 candidates) keyed by model family and latency budget, and 3) unit-economics telemetry surfaced in the Redwood Optimize UI and CLI so customers can see estimated $/1k tokens for each profile. Design highlights: heuristic-based defaults avoid risky global changes; profiles are opt-in and annotated with expected quality regressions and fallback rules; unit-econ computes marginal cost using current node pricing and observed token throughput. Changeset summary: changes in serving runtime and config, new autotune coordinator service, additional metrics and tracing hooks, updates to the Optimize tooling and docs, and tests. Checklist: - [x] Implement default heuristics and profiles - [x] Add unit-econ sampling and aggregation - [x] Wire metrics to Optimize UI - [x] Add integration tests and load test harness - [x] Add docs and migration notes Testing notes: validated on perf-canary with 5 representative workloads (chat, completion, embeddings, rerank, structured-output). Observed median cost reduction 18% for chat workloads, tail latency within SLOs after conservative throttles applied. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag per-tenant; defaults off for customers with custom configs. Linear refs: ENG-1942 implements the autotune coordinator; ENG-2087 adds quant profiles; PM-633 scopes Optimize UX changes. See files changed for scope and commit list below.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Overall LGTM, left a few nits around config naming and doc clarity.
Sofia Patel: responded: renamed keys to follow kebab-case and clarified the fallback rules in the docs per comments.

Aisha Thompson: question: how do we surface quality regressions for int4 profiles? reply: added an annotation field in profiles.yaml and the Optimize UI will show example eval deltas and a 'recommended' flag.

Rafael Gomez: requested change: add a safety throttle to avoid aggressive quant picks on cold-start traffic. Sofia: implemented a cooldown window in coordinator and added unit tests + perf-canary scenario.
